report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** High-quality randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials show that *pharmaceutical-grade oral cannabidiol* added to existing antiseizure therapy reduces convulsive-seizure frequency in children/adolescents with treatment-resistant Dravet syndrome.

In the pivotal 120-patient trial (ages 2–18), cannabidiol 20 mg/kg/day produced a median **39% reduction** in monthly convulsive seizures versus **13% with placebo** over the treatment period. A later 199-child dose-ranging trial replicated benefit: median reductions were **48.7% (10 mg/kg/day)** and **45.7% (20 mg/kg/day)**, versus **26.9%** with placebo; 10 mg/kg/day was better tolerated.

This evidence applies to the regulated prescription formulation (Epidiolex/Epidyolex), as an add-on—not to over-the-counter CBD products, whose dose, purity, and evidence base differ. Important adverse effects include sleepiness, diarrhea, reduced appetite, and liver-enzyme elevations; monitoring and interaction review (especially with clobazam and valproate) are needed. The FDA indication covers seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients aged ≥2 years.
